chunks: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning:

A woman for whom dawn rises while she is menstruating in the month of Ramadan, then when morning comes she becomes pure, and she has already eaten, then she performs the Zuhr and ʿAsr salat (prayer)—what should she do regarding that day in which she became pure? He عليه السلام said: She should fast, but she should not count it.

key_terms.الْفَجْرُ: dawn, the beginning of the fasting day
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan in which fasting is obligatory
key_terms.صَلَّتِ الظُّهْرَ وَالْعَصْرَ: she performed the Zuhr and ʿAsr salat (prayer)
key_terms.لَا تَعْتَدُّ بِهِ: she should not count that day as a valid fast

ai.seo_question: What should a woman do if she becomes pure from menstruation after dawn in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a menstruating woman who becomes pure during the daytime in the month of Ramadan after dawn has already broken. She is instructed to observe fasting for the remainder of the day, but that day does not count as a valid fast of Ramadan.
